purpose: Re-gate source 1 with the fixed integrity_scan.py. Its original gate 5 pass came from the version that globbed *.json and never opened non-JSON files.
verdict: FAIL - unexpected_domains is non-empty. Benign in substance (see assessment) but the gate criterion is not met, so no status was changed and the snapshot was not touched.

assessment.facebook.github.io: One occurrence, in .git/hooks/fsmonitor-watchman.sample - a stock file shipped with every git installation, linking to the Watchman docs. Not third-party content from the data source.
assessment.dot_git_directory_present: 33 files under .git/, invisible to the previous *.json-globbing gate. Includes a live remote (https://github.com/StarCitizenWiki/scunpacked-data.git) and pack objects.
assessment.active_git_hooks_assessment: All four read (reading is permitted; executing is not). Verbatim stock Git LFS hooks, 350-360 bytes each, installed locally by git lfs install during the clone. Each shells out to git lfs <verb>. Nothing injected, nothing authored by the data source.
assessment.implication: The snapshot is not inert: a git pull inside that folder would mutate data described as an immutable snapshot, and the LFS hooks fire on git operations. Whether .git belongs in a data snapshot is an open decision - and removal would mean moving it to _to_delete/, never deleting.

per_file_report: 01_integrity_scan_perfile.json - 10.4 MB, gitignored as regenerable; re-run integrity_scan.py against the same path to reproduce it.
